sections.overview: The Lesser Snouted Treefrog is widespread in the southern part of South America, from Bolivia and Brazil to Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina.
sections.identification: It has a flattened, triangular snout, prominent eyes and a variable pale dorsal pattern.
sections.habitat: It uses open and wooded habitats, including altered areas, often near water.
sections.diet: Adult diet is not detailed in the sources reviewed.
sections.behavior: Males call from branches and shrubs and may shelter under bark near water.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs in water, where tadpoles develop; breeding seasons vary among populations.
sections.ecology: In Corrientes, Argentina, it was recorded as a prolonged breeder, while other studies report different seasonal patterns in other regions.
sections.conservation: The Argentine biodiversity information system reports Least Concern globally and not threatened under national assessments; these categories apply at different scales.
